title: Dominica and Saint Lucia checked
text: Dominica: the VAT registration level was corrected from EC$300,000 to EC$250,000, the level published by the Inland Revenue Division. Saint Lucia: the VAT registration level was corrected from EC$180,000 to EC$400,000, as shown on most pages of the tax office site, and the 2023 income tax table (EC$25,000 allowance, 15%, 20%, 30%) was confirmed on a government document.

title: Antigua and Barbuda and Saint Kitts and Nevis checked
text: Antigua and Barbuda: the EC$300,000 ABST registration level was confirmed on the tax office site, with the early-registration rule and the absence of a registration fee. Saint Kitts and Nevis: the VAT registration level was corrected from EC$400,000 to EC$150,000 for goods (EC$96,000 for certain services) after several sources agreed, and a note now mentions the unincorporated business tax of about 4%.

title: Jamaica and Guyana checked
text: Jamaica: the J$1,902,360 tax-free amount from April 2026 was confirmed and the April 2027 rise to about J$2,003,496 is now noted. Guyana: the NIS site confirms that the self-employed pay 12.5% of declared income; the 14% seen in other sources is the combined rate for employed people.

title: Bonaire, Saba and Sint Eustatius checked
text: The 2026 income tax figures (29.4% up to US$53,198, then 38.4%, tax-free allowance US$21,956) and the ABB rates were confirmed on the Caribbean Netherlands tax office site. New note: sole traders with sales under US$30,000 a year can ask for an ABB exemption, and the ABB is declared every quarter.

title: Haiti and US Virgin Islands checked
text: Haiti: the fixed patente of G 1,250, G 2,500 or G 5,000 by commune group was confirmed on the DGI site, and a note now explains that a new business pays only the fixed G 5,000 in its first period. US Virgin Islands: the US$390 yearly business licence renewal was confirmed on the DLCA site; the 2026 federal-based tax figures were re-read.

title: Trinidad and Tobago and Barbados checked
text: Trinidad and Tobago: the TT$90,000 personal allowance and the 16.2% National Insurance rate for 2026 were confirmed; the rate is reported to rise to 19.2% in January 2027. Barbados: the VAT threshold rise to BDS$350,000 from 1 October 2026 is reported by two sources, not yet confirmed by the tax authority.

title: Share tools and partner kit
text: Share buttons, social images, QR codes, printable flyers and a four-language partner kit for organisations.

title: US Virgin Islands
text: The US Virgin Islands were added. The French West Indies link to the French version of Pa a Pa.

title: Sint Maarten, Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba
text: Four Dutch-language territories were added in English and Dutch. Sint Maarten uses the 2025 income tax table until the 2026 table is confirmed.

title: Dutch interface
text: A Dutch interface was added for Aruba, Curaçao and Suriname.

title: French interface and Haiti
text: A French interface was added with Haiti.

title: Aruba, Curaçao, Suriname and Haiti
text: Four countries were added in English.

title: British territories
text: The Cayman Islands, British Virgin Islands, Turks and Caicos, Anguilla and Montserrat were added.

title: Eastern Caribbean social security rates
text: Social security rates for Saint Lucia, Dominica, Grenada, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, Antigua and Barbuda and Saint Kitts and Nevis were updated from official sources.

title: Guides for search engines and AI assistants
text: Each country has a static guide page, with a sitemap and an llms.txt file.

title: Spanish interface
text: A Spanish interface was added for the Dominican Republic, Puerto Rico and Cuba.

title: English version
text: The English version launched with Jamaica, then Trinidad and Tobago, Guyana, Barbados, The Bahamas and Belize.
